business_problem: Engine needed a voice-support experience that could answer traveler questions, manage bookings, and handle hotel cancellations at scale without sounding robotic or forcing callers to repeat themselves to human agents.
solution_summary: Engine launched a customer-facing voice-support workflow on Salesforce with Agentforce Voice at the front end and Agentforce for Service behind the scenes so high-volume travel calls can be handled conversationally. Because Engine's stack was already described as 'wall-to-wall Salesforce,' the project could use native CRM, customer-record, and service context instead of bolting a separate voice layer onto fragmented systems. NeuraFlash, Engine, and Salesforce iterated rapidly before and after general availability, testing live conversations, refining prompts and voice settings, and rolling traffic out in phases from 10% of calls to 50% and then 75%. When the AI cannot finish the task, the transfer includes a completed transcript and summary inside Agentforce for Service, which shortens handoffs, preserves traveler context, and lets reps focus on exceptions instead of re-collecting information.
data_flow: Incoming traveler calls are answered by Agentforce Voice, which uses CRM and Data 360 context to answer questions or complete tasks; if the workflow needs a human, the call is transferred into Agentforce for Service with a full transcript and AI summary already attached.
business_outcome: Engine scaled voice support with a more human-sounding agent, rolled the system out to most inbound calls, and simplified rep work by handing off completed voice transcripts and summaries instead of forcing customers to restart the conversation.
architecture_clues: Engine described its environment as 'wall-to-wall Salesforce,' which reduced integration friction.
